metadata.title: Gated exciton fluids: a proof that image charges preserve complete monotonicity, a driven-dissipative solver test on rusty-SUNDIALS, and a laboratory protocol
metadata.description: Follow-up to the author's first note on a planar lattice-optimality theorem and an exciton-fluid interaction (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23289027). (1) A proof (paper and pencil; not formalised in Lean) that for grounded perfect-conductor gates at arbitrary distances and arbitrary layer positions, the dipolar exciton-exciton kernel built from the image-charge series is completely monotone in r^2: its Laplace measure is a sum of terms 2(1-cos(b-a))(1+cos(a+b)) >= 0 after Poisson summation. Within that model the gates cannot be engineered to break the hypothesis of the (unrefereed, AI-generated) lattice theorem. The independent review of this note supplied a spectral argument extending the statement to layered dielectrics, reported as a remark, not a full proof. The zero-wavevector coefficient 4 pi d (1 - d/D) is a textbook capacitor formula. (2) A pre-registered numerical test on the author's Rust implementation of CVODE (rusty-SUNDIALS) of a generic driven-dissipative Gross-Pitaevskii model with an incoherent reservoir and a gate potential: steady states, the 768x768 linearisation, the conservative limit, the ARKode-style IMEX module (a fixed-point implicit stage that errors where h*gamma_R*a_ii exceeds 1; second order below) and a planted bug passed as registered; the stationarity and pump-budget gates of the gate sweep failed as registered at t = 4000 (the horizon was too short) and pass in an exploratory continuation to t = 16000, one seed per amplitude. The gate sweep ran on an 8x8 grid because the registered cost was misjudged by two orders of magnitude; in that small periodic box the emission shift is only the area average of the gate. Three amendments preceded the numbers they affect, a fourth was recorded while the last run was in progress, and one registered comparison (sorted eigenvalue lists) was replaced by a nearest-neighbour matching without an amendment; all are disclosed. (3) A laboratory protocol (L1-L6) with expected outcomes, pass/fail rules and confounders, stating which items can fail (only the dependence of the interaction strength on gate separation) and which are calibrations or controls. Not done: Lean formalisation, the Wigner-crystallisation transition, edges and frustration, any Hugging Face data or neural-network surrogate, any comparison with data; no claim about exciton Bose-Einstein condensation; the model parameters are dimensionless and chosen for solver stiffness. Written by an AI system; reviewed by another instance of the same model family and briefly by the author; not refereed; no experimental group has seen it.
